LESSON: LISTENING AND SPEAKING 1.1.1 ATTENTIVE LISTENING

Grade: Grade 4
Subject: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES
Strand: Strand 1
Topic 1.1: Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Attentive Listening

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Attentive Listening. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: How should we respond to instructions?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify nouns in singular and plural forms from a song for information
2. respond to verbal instructions for information
3. appreciate listening to various cultural songs for information

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: LISTENING AND SPEAKING 1.1.1 ATTENTIVE LISTENING
Subject: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES · Grade: Grade 4
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Attentive Listening helps you succeed in INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: LISTENING AND SPEAKING 1.1.1 ATTENTIVE LISTENING
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Identify nouns in singular and plural forms from a song for information

What this means
In this part you learn to identify nouns in singular and plural forms from a song for information. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify nouns in singular and plural forms from a song for information.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Attentive Listening”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify nouns in singular and plural forms from a song for information. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Respond to verbal instructions for information

What this means
In this part you learn to respond to verbal instructions for information. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: respond to verbal instructions for information.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model speaking: Say 4 clear sentences about Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Attentive Listening to a partner.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can respond to verbal instructions for information. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Appreciate listening to various cultural songs for information

What this means
In this part you learn to appreciate listening to various cultural songs for information. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: appreciate listening to various cultural songs for information.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model writing: Write 5 neat sentences using new words from this lesson.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can appreciate listening to various cultural songs for information. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Attentive Listening is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Attentive Listening”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: identify nouns in singular and plural forms from a song for information)

Example 2: Say 4 clear sentences about Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Attentive Listening to a partner. (skill: respond to verbal instructions for information)

Example 3: Write 5 neat sentences using new words from this lesson. (skill: appreciate listening to various cultural songs for information)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Attentive Listening to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: identify nouns in singular and plural forms from a song for information.
3. Practise this skill: respond to verbal instructions for information.
4. Practise this skill: appreciate listening to various cultural songs for information.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Attentive Listening from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Attentive Listening: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 4 learner study Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Attentive Listening?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. How should we respond to instructions?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Attentive Listening means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: identify nouns in singular and plural forms from a song for information.
5. Be able to: respond to verbal instructions for information.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
